title: Epistemic Past Modals: Foresight and Foreseeability

sections.title: What Could or Ought to Have Been Known
sections.content: When cognitive verbs like 'tud' (know), 'sejt' (suspect/sense), 'észrevesz' (notice), and 'előre lát' (foresee) take the past potential + 'volna', they express epistemic hindsight: whether an agent had sufficient clues to foresee a crisis ('Tudhatta volna, hogy veszélyes' = He could/should have known it was dangerous; 'Senki sem láthatta előre' = Nobody could have foreseen it).

sections.title: Definite vs. Indefinite Conjugation with Hindsight
sections.content: Because these verbs usually govern a 'hogy'-clause or a specific object ('a bajt', 'az igazságot'), they typically take the definite conjugation: 'tudhatta volna' (he could have known it), 'sejthettük volna' (we could have suspected it), 'észrevehették volna' (they could have noticed it).

sections.title: Epistemic Hindsight Forms
rows: Tudhatta volna, hogy a láz visszatér.
He/she could (should) have known that the fever would return.
Sejthettük volna, hogy nagyobb a baj.
We could have suspected that the trouble was greater.
Hamarabb is észrevehette volna a jeleket.
He/she could have noticed the signs sooner.
Senki sem láthatta előre a következményeket.
Nobody could have foreseen the consequences.

items.spanish: Nelli tudhatta volna, hogy a hangos jókedv mögött súlyos gyengeség lappang.
items.english: Nelli could have known that severe weakness was lurking behind the loud cheerfulness.

items.spanish: A korabeli orvosok is észrevehették volna az összefüggést a higiénia és a láz között.
items.english: Contemporary doctors too could have noticed the connection between hygiene and fever.

items.spanish: A betegség ilyen gyors lefolyását senki sem láthatta előre.
items.english: Nobody could have foreseen such a rapid course of the illness.

sections.title: B2 Stylistic Notice
sections.content: In negative sentences with 'senki sem' (nobody), 'láthatta előre' does not need 'volna' when stating an objective historical impossibility ('senki sem láthatta előre' = nobody could foresee it), or adds 'volna' for counterfactual nuance.
